text: Have you ever noticed that elephants have huge fan-like ears, while a snake seems to have no ears at all? Can a snake still hear? Let's solve the mystery of animal ears!
What would happen if a tiny mouse had the huge ears of an elephant? Why do you think different animals have different types of ears?

content.title: Types of Animal Ears
content.description: See how elephants use big ears like fans, and birds have tiny holes covered with feathers.

text: Some animals have ears we can see on the outside, called external ears. Others, like birds and lizards, have tiny holes on the sides of their heads covered by feathers or scales! Their ears are hidden.

content.description: Ears that are visible on the outside of the body.
Ears that are hidden inside the head or just small holes, usually covered by feathers or scales.

content.question: Which of these animals has ears that we can clearly see on the outside?

content.text: Many students think that birds and snakes are completely deaf because they don't have visible ears. But they can hear very well! Birds have small ear holes hidden under feathers, and snakes feel vibrations on the ground.

text: Think about your pet dog or cat, or a cow you saw on the street. Can you see their ears? How are their ears different from a crow's? Take a moment to reflect.

Ears aren't just for hearing! Elephants use their large ears to cool themselves down in the hot sun. Animals' bodies are perfectly adapted to their environment. This is a beautiful connection to nature's design!

content.text: Look around your neighborhood today. Make a list of 5 animals whose ears you can see and 3 animals whose ears you cannot see. Draw them in your notebook!

text: Imagine a magical rule that can tell you if an animal lays eggs or gives birth to babies, just by looking at its face! Do you want to know the secret?
Think about a dog and a hen. A dog has babies, and a hen lays eggs. What is the main difference you see on their heads and bodies? Predict the secret rule!

content.title: The Ear and Hair Rule
content.description: Animals with visible ears and body hair give birth to babies. Animals with hidden ears lay eggs!

text: The Secret Rule: Animals that have visible ears and hair on their body give birth to young ones. Animals that do not have visible ears on the outside (and usually have feathers or scales) lay eggs!

content.description: Animals that give birth to young ones. They usually have visible ears and body hair.
Animals that lay eggs. They usually do not have visible ears and have feathers, scales, or smooth skin.

content.text: Ask students to touch their own ears and hair. Since humans have both, we also give birth to babies! This makes the concept instantly relatable.

content.question: A crocodile does not have visible ears on the outside and has scales. Based on our secret rule, does it lay eggs or give birth to babies?

text: Explain this secret rule to your parents! Ask them if a cow gives birth to babies or lays eggs, and then explain how they can know just by looking at the cow's ears.

This rule connects to Biology and the classification of mammals. Almost all mammals have hair and visible ears, and they feed milk to their babies! Our ancient texts also observe how animals that give birth have similar features.

content.text: Draw two animals: one that has hair and visible ears, and one that has scales/feathers and hidden ears. Label them as 'Lays Eggs' or 'Gives Birth'. This is your mastery challenge!
